title: A Confirmatory Paired Evaluation of Generate→Verify→Repair vs LLM‑Only NetOps Suggestions: A Reproducible Ceiling/Null Result
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) comparing a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipeline against accepting an LLM suggestion directly for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using deterministic task selection and a shared single generator candidate per task, K=200 tasks were evaluated with a single requested model (gpt-5-mini). Observed primary outcome: baseline = 200/200 validator‑compliant applies; guarded = 200/200; paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00]. The repair step was never invoked. The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis H1 (that G→V→R reduces regression‑causing changes versus LLM‑only) is not supported under the tested sampling/model/validator regime. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived and hashed for deterministic replay (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4233332164d0453e2aecdb34d52a01883358d67ac30e028e6). The exact initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). We discuss operational implications, reproducibility, and experimental contracts for future failure‑rich follow‑ups.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation with generative models promises operational efficiency but carries risk: erroneous changes can create outages, violate policies, or cause dependency regressions. A common architecture to mitigate risk is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): an LLM proposes candidates, a deterministic verifier checks safety/policy, and an automated repair step attempts fixes before apply. Despite active community interest and many prototypes advocating this pattern, there is little preregistered, artifact‑archived causal evidence quantifying the verifier/repair marginal effect under deterministic, reproducible selection rules. We therefore preregistered (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) and executed a paired experiment that isolates the verifier+repair marginal effect while holding the generator output fixed per task. Research question: To what extent does an iterative G→V→R pipeline reduce regression‑causing network changes compared to accepting an LLM suggestion directly? Principal contributions: (1) a fully preregistered, deterministic paired evaluation (K=200) with complete artifact hashing and provenance for bit‑exact replay; (2) a reproducible ceiling/null result under the declared experimental contract (no discordant pairs; repairs unused); and (3) concrete, artifact‑grounded guidance for designing failure‑rich next experiments.
sections.related_work: Recent work has converged on generate→validate→repair and tool‑augmented agentic NetOps workflows that place formal or deterministic verifiers next to generative models to bound risk (examples and system prototypes are widely discussed in recent NetOps/AIops literature; see Cornetto, TypoNet, and other generate–validate–repair position papers). Benchmarks such as Cornetto articulate the evaluation need for functional verification across realistic topologies. Our study differs by preregistering a paired estimand with deterministic selection and by publishing the complete execution and analysis manifests to support bit‑exact independent replay.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design. The study was preregistered in machine‑readable form (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop; preregistration SHA‑256 = a6d73a5cc0bda22e691a3634068a881b36ae274a65ab33919a647ec32c56e622) and fixed all scientific choices prior to observation: paired design with two conditions per task (baseline: accept LLM proposal; guarded: run deterministic verifier and allow at most one automated repair if verifier fails), a single shared_initial_generation per task so that the paired contrast isolates the verifier+repair marginal effect, deterministic selection of tasks (K=200) from an assembled public pool by computing SHA‑256(intent_string) and selecting the first 200 hashes, inclusion only of intents for which the preregistered verifier reported coverage, maximum_model_calls = 400, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1, and the primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Model/configuration and tools. Requested model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Deterministic verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Execution and artifact capture. The autonomous pipeline preserved all prompts, model outputs, provider call traces, per‑episode scoring JSONs, verifier traces, deterministic selection manifests, and per‑file SHA‑256 fingerprints (see artifact table). Key archived fingerprints include: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...), and execution/transformation_manifest.json (SHA‑256 = 79c91155...). Analysis plan. Primary confirmatory test: exact McNemar two‑sided test on paired binary outcomes with paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) to produce a 95% percentile CI; analysis executor = paired_binary_analysis_v1. Missingness and contamination rules were preregistered; no exclusions or missing episodes occurred.
sections.results: Execution summary. Planned episodes: 400 (2 arms × 200 tasks). Completed episodes: 400. Model calls used: 200 (one shared generator call per task); repair calls invoked: 0 (repair_applied = false for all tasks). Primary outcome. Paired contingency counts: n11 (both success) = 200; n10 (guarded success only) = 0; n01 (baseline success only) = 0; n00 (both fail) = 0. Observed rates: baseline_success_rate = 200/200 = 1.0; guarded_success_rate = 200/200 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00. Inferential statistics: exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI for paired difference = [0.00, 0.00]. Representative episode diagnostics. Every execution/scoring JSON embeds deterministic validator diagnostics enabling audit: parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, final_state snapshot, and validator.violation_count. Example archived scoring JSONs: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 = 3055f874cebd979af0ded1859e51e6f51d937b5f9967d62c73f439aa52a257cc) and execution/scoring/task-000003-guarded.json (SHA‑256 = d10b415a1974c9ba846a31a0392edee2f117bae1a83411c984bed2d1d6c9411b) — both are provided in the artifact bundle and contain the per‑task validator traces used to score validity.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis H1 (that G→V→R reduces regression‑causing applies versus LLM‑only) was not supported under the tested regime: both arms produced validator‑compliant applies for every selected task and the repair pathway was never invoked. This outcome is a reproducible ceiling/null result given the preregistered sampling, model, and validator. It does not imply that verifiers are universally unnecessary. Key methodological inferences and operational implications: (1) Inclusion filter effect — tasks were included only if the preregistered verifier reported coverage; this policy intentionally reduced the prevalence of verifier failures in the sampled pool and thus produced a failure‑poor sample. (2) Shared_initial_generation isolates verifier marginality — by fixing the generator candidate per task the paired contrast measures the incremental impact of verifier+repair on the same candidate, but it prevents generator adaptation (regeneration) after verifier feedback; an end‑to‑end operational pipeline would plausibly allow generator regeneration and thus measure a different estimand. (3) Model‑validator pairing specificity — results depend on the requested model (gpt-5-mini) and the deterministic validator implementation; other pairings can produce different outcomes. (4) Cost accounting — because repairs were not invoked the measured model call cost equals number of tasks (200); provider call traces and per‑call hashes permit exact token/cost accounting for alternative replay. Reproducibility and audit. All artifacts needed for deterministic replay are archived and hashed: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...), execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce9255...), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...), and provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e...). Researchers can reconstruct the paired outcomes deterministically by re‑parsing the execution/scoring/*.json artifacts referenced in the manifest.
sections.conclusion: In a fully preregistered, deterministic paired evaluation (K=200; shared_initial_generation per task; requested_model=gpt-5-mini), both baseline and guarded arms achieved 200/200 validator‑compliant applies. The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis H1 — that G→V→R reduces regression‑causing changes relative to accepting an LLM suggestion directly — was not supported in the tested sampling/model/validator regime (paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar p = 1.00; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00]). The repair pathway was never exercised. This ceiling/null result is reproducible from the archived artifacts (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce9255...; provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 = 1872df1e...). For future work we recommend deliberately sampling failure‑rich intents, evaluating closed‑loop generator–validator estimands that allow regeneration upon validator failure, and reporting aggregated task‑difficulty and validator‑coverage summaries (per‑episode difficulty labels are present in the archived execution/scoring/*.json and execution/task_manifest.jsonl and permit deterministic aggregation). All artifacts required to reproduce or to re‑analyze alternative estimands are archived and hashed for audit and independent analysis.

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (requested_model = gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize to other LLMs without additional experiments.

Task pool inclusion required preregistered verifier coverage; this biased the sample toward intents the verifier already supports and reduced external validity to failure‑rich production distributions.
Construct validity depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; validator blind spots would render the binary outcome an imperfect proxy for true operational regressions.

Shared_initial_generation fixes generator output across arms and prevents closed‑loop generator adaptation; the experiment therefore measures verifier marginality on fixed candidates rather than end‑to‑end adaptive improvement.
Observed ceiling (baseline success = 100%) made the preregistered power assumption inapplicable; inference is descriptive and bounded to the archived sampling/model regime.

This revision step did not add an aggregated summary table of task difficulty counts because the execution preserved per‑episode difficulty labels in execution/scoring/*.json and execution/task_manifest.jsonl but did not produce an aggregated summary during the autonomous run; the per‑episode artifacts contain the required fields and permit deterministic aggregation by independent auditors (see artifact fingerprints listed in the manuscript).
